title: AnaDiffusion: Anatomically Compositional Latent Diffusion for Controllable 3D Brain MRI Generation
claim: Monolithic baselines show local structural artifacts; composing parts then refining yields coherent outputs and better scores across regions.
layout: 3 zones left-to-right: baseline vs ours image columns with zoom insets, radar charts
description: The left and center show a side-by-side comparison. A column of three brain MRI slices (coronal, sagittal, axial) is labeled 'Baselines' on the left, and a matching column labeled 'AnaDiffusion' is on the right. Between them, a dashed trapezoid with magnifier icons holds three color-coded failure labels: pink 'Left-right structural inconsistency', yellow 'Inter-part discontinuity' and green 'Structural boundary collapse'. Each label has two zoomed crops of baseline artifacts. On the far right, two radar charts show MedicalNet FID (five axes) and SynthSeg Cohen's |d| (four axes). Many dashed or dotted baseline lines sit near the centre. A bold red 'Ours' polygon covers the outer boundary. A legend sits at the bottom right. The eye goes first to the brain images and then to the red polygons.
caption: AnaDiffusion for anatomically compositional 3D brain MRI generation. Unlike monolithic baselines (left) that may suffer from left-right inconsistency, inter-part discontinuity, and boundary collapse, AnaDiffusion generates part-specific anatomical assets and refines their assembled scaffold into a coherent whole-brain volume. The radar charts (right) summarize Table 1: each axis is min--max normalized on a log scale and lower-is-better metrics (FID, |d|) are inverted, so points farther from the centre are better.
abstract: 3D brain MRI generation has made significant advances in medical imaging, simulation, and controllable anatomical analysis. However, existing generative models typically synthesize 3D volumes monolithically, often overlooking regional anatomical structures and limiting local controllability. To address these limitations, we introduce AnaDiffusion, an anatomically compositional latent diffusion framework that factorizes the generation process into distinct, anatomically meaningful regions, followed by part-to-whole assembly and global refinement. Our approach first trains part diffusion models to capture local structural priors. We then inject an assembled anatomical composite of the parts into the whole-brain latent representation and continue denoising. This mechanism enables the model to resolve global context while preserving the injected anatomy. AnaDiffusion thus produces explicit part assets and a globally coherent volume, enabling controllable part editing without subject-specific dense segmentation maps at inference. On a subject-disjoint ADNI test split, AnaDiffusion attains the lowest mean FrÃ©chet distance (FID) in every evaluated region. In localized editing, it achieves substantially higher target transfer (paired MS-SSIM) than a segmentation-conditioned baseline, with off-target preservation close to the baseline's.
